did_you_know.text: Instead of one continuous territory, the Levites received cities within the lands of the other tribes. The Book of Numbers lists 48 Levitical cities.
The three gifts mentioned here are called priestly gifts in Jewish tradition. They come from specific parts of a slaughtered animal, not from all of its meat.
“The first shearing” became the legal term for the gift taken from the flock’s first shearing. The verse thus brings together crops, wine, oil, and an animal product.

The phrase “passing his son or daughter through fire” is generally understood as involving children in a fire ritual connected with human sacrifice. The Torah places it alongside various forms of divination and magic.
The prophet described here must be “from among your brothers”—a member of Israel, not a foreign prophet. This offers a way to seek God’s word without turning to diviners.
Horeb is another name for Mount Sinai in the biblical tradition. It was the place of the great revelation where the people asked not to hear God’s voice directly.

The verse gives a practical test for a prophet’s words: if the prediction does not come true, it should not be attributed to God. The ending, “do not fear him,” reminds us not to be automatically intimidated by someone claiming prophetic authority.
